expectations.text: The absence of a named evening owner is identified as decisive: with nobody free to own it, every organised-evening option is off the table.
expectations.evidence: "If no one can own an evening, every rung above 'no organised programme' is deleted. Five people fully committed... means no owner."

expectations.text: The recommendation is 'no organised programme' published as the decision, or any organised option is made conditional on first naming an owner with real capacity.
expectations.evidence: "Recommendation: option (b)... The day ends at 17:30, with no organised evening, and you publish that now."

expectations.text: The boat cruise is rejected, and it is ranked below running nothing at all.
expectations.evidence: "The skill ranks the offsite excursion below doing nothing."

expectations.text: The cruise rejection cites the 80-seat boat excluding most of the 220, or the headcount being uncorrectable once transport leaves.
expectations.evidence: "The boat takes 80 and two rotations cover at most 160 of 220."

expectations.text: The excursion is stated to earn its place only when it is the event's signature moment and the whole audience fits it - neither true here.
expectations.evidence: "The skill allows an excursion only if it's the event's signature moment and the whole audience fits. Neither is true here."

expectations.text: The pub-drift option is rejected: it looks like a free mixer but is the version with nobody responsible.
expectations.evidence: "'We'll all end up at the Anchor' is the unhosted drift... It looks like a free mixer, but it has no owner."

expectations.text: The drift's specific risk is named: conduct-policy scope is weakest exactly where the unhosted evening happens.
expectations.evidence: "The code-of-conduct scope is also weakest there, because the pub isn't your space."

expectations.text: The absence is published: the schedule states the day ends at the last session, early enough for attendees to plan their own evening.
expectations.evidence: "Publish early... soon enough that people can plan their own evening."

expectations.text: A distinction is drawn between a published absence, which is legitimate, and silence, which is the failure people fill themselves.
expectations.evidence: "The failure is the silence, not the absence."

expectations.text: Running the evening half-heartedly is warned against as the same drift with the event's name attached.
expectations.evidence: No warning about a half-run evening or drift with the event's branding appears anywhere in the transcript.

expectations.text: The venue-based mixer is identified as the default evening format if an owner ever exists: the event's own space, right after the last session, with no travel or cost to attend.
expectations.evidence: "The upgrade path is a venue-based mixer... right after 17:30, in your own space... free, open to every badge."

expectations.text: The evening decision is handed to the conduct-policy owner for the scope question rather than settled here.
